title: Revolved flanged hub with a driven bore and six mounting holes
intent: Turn one closed stepped section into a coaxial solid; drill one central bore and one mounting seed; pattern the seed feature; revise two user parameters and measure every dependent hole.

ops.name: Six mounting holes on 60 mm PCD

check: Run lane_preflight on ops, then tee_batch(adapter='fusion', ops=ops) in a separate empty parametric design. Retain the actual body ID from the diff and use fu_measure(of=that ID), fu_design_stats and fu_params. Expect one solid, four healthy features, bbox [32,80,80] mm and volume 20816*pi mm3. Inspect cylindrical faces: the central bore is radius 6 mm; exactly six inner cylinders of radius 3 mm have the stated centres projected to the x=0 plane. This separates real drilled holes from outside cylindrical faces. Compare STEP readback against these analytic dimensions and volume.

revision.check: Run the revision in the same document after creation. User parameter values must be 16 mm and 8 mm, with the original hole feature expressions still naming those parameters. The central bore must grow to radius 8 mm and all six mounting holes to radius 4 mm without creating or deleting a feature. Body bounds stay [32,80,80] mm and volume becomes 19584*pi mm3, a decrease of 1232*pi mm3. Recheck every cylinder centre and feature health; export and read back this revised solid.

lessons: A six-line profile lies in XY; x is its length coordinate and y its radius. Its boundary touches the x axis and its interior never crosses it. A 360-degree x-axis revolve therefore produces one stepped solid.
The mounting seed starts on the unique -x face at x=0. For face -x, a two-coordinate at:[30,0] means world y=30,z=0; this avoids accidentally picking the farther +x hub end at x=32.
Set a hole feature's expression to the user parameter before creating the circular pattern. A later param_set then changes the seed and every patterned copy.
The circular pattern count includes the seed. Six instances at a full 360 degrees give distinct positions separated by 60 degrees.
Pattern the mounting-hole feature only. Patterning the revolve or central bore would duplicate coincident geometry.
A successful call is a claim; removed volume, individual bore centres and independent STEP readback are the evidence.
limits: Use a separate empty parametric document with unused A79F_ parameter names. Existing bodies would contaminate whole-design measurement and through-hole scope.
The body and patterned feature must remain native to the root component; the x-axis pattern passes through the root origin.
Aliases are valid only inside the creation batch. The separate revision uses user parameter names and needs no guessed entity IDs.
The stepped outline uses explicit numeric coordinates; the driven revision covers the two bore diameters. This lesson does not claim a fully constrained section sketch.
Fillets, threads, taps and manufacturing fit are outside this example. The geometry is intentionally sharp so its exact volume is independently defensible.
Replace /absolute/output with an existing absolute output directory. STEP and F3D export the design, so omit of rather than supplying a body ID.
